newsitem.title: GERMANY: Trichet sees "euro" stability pact by year-end.
newsitem.headline: Trichet sees "euro" stability pact by year-end.

text.p: French central bank governor Jean-claude Trichet said on Tuesday he expected a "euro" stability pact to be ready by the end of the year.
"I think we will certainly deliver (by) the end of the year a nice, appropriate stability pact," Trichet told Reuters Financial Television after a Franco-German economic summit here.

"I think it's very important that we have a good agreement between Germany and France and, of course, all others in Europe in order to ensure the credibility of the ECB (European central bank), the credibility of the euro and to ensure credibility of our currency, our long-term rates, medium-term rates, market rates, today of course" Trichet said.
"Credibility is absolutely key, not only now but also in the medium and long run," Trichet said.

French finance minister Jean Arthuis earlier said after the same summit that France and Germany had agreed on the need for a "stability council" on monetary union where those who moved to the "euro" could oversee application of the stability pact.
Trichet said earlier at a news conference that the stability pact would help boost confidence in the future single currency.

"We are very very happy to see the agreement between Mr Arthuis and Mr (German Finance Minister Theo) Waigel on the idea of the stability pact and the stability council because it seems that it is a major factor in confidence in the future" of the single currency, he said.
